title: Six Ten at the Swing Bridge
subject: A swing-bridge keeper on a small river turns the span open at 6:10 every morning for one coal barge, knows its pilot only by her two horn blasts and a lamp, and today leaves the bridge open and walks down to the quay with two cups of tea.
caption: Motorik krautrock-pop, 1970s German motorik beat with a warm melodic top line. Relentless motorik 4/4 drum beat with steady hi-hat and snare on two and four, pulsing eighth-note bass guitar, chiming clean guitar with light delay, analogue string-synth pad, simple repeating organ line. Spacious dry analogue studio mix, slight tape flutter, steady forward drive. Male tenor, calm and even, plain delivery. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 128 BPM, D minor. Hypnotic, steady, quietly warm. No rap, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no distorted guitars, no heavy modern bass drops, no vocal effects.
lyrics:
[Intro - motorik drums, pulsing bass, chiming guitar]

[Verse 1]
Ten past six, I turn the key
The iron span begins to swing
A coal barge rounds the river bend
Two horn blasts and the water sings

[Pre-Chorus]
I have never heard her name
I know her lamp, I know her wave

[Chorus]
Open the bridge, let the morning through
Two long blasts, I know it's you
Every day I turn it round
Open the bridge, let the morning through

[Verse 2]
Four years of tea gone cold up here
I log the hour, I log the weight
The barge slides under, slow and low
She tips her cap, she never waits

[Pre-Chorus]
I have never heard her name
Today I walk down there

[Chorus]
Open the bridge, let the morning through
Two long blasts, I know it's you
I leave the span out wide and stay
Open the bridge, let the morning through

[Bridge - bass and drums only]
Two cups of tea, one set of stairs

[Chorus]
Open the bridge, let the morning through
Two long blasts, and I walk down to you
The river holds the bridge apart
Open the bridge, let the morning through

[Outro - organ, drums drive on]
Ten past six, ten past six
